statement: h11's memory (mem-h11-0002) documented that `enforcer-scan/src/walk.rs`'s `glob_matches` only strips a SINGLE trailing/leading `*`, so a repo-relative exclude glob must be written as `<dir>/*` (single star, matching prefix), never `<dir>/**` — a `**` entry silently degrades to a literal-asterisk suffix check and never matches anything. h12 needed to exclude `crates/enforcer-harness/adapters/**` (the workpack's own prose used `**`) from the `ocentra-enforcer` profile's `ignoreFileGlobs`; following h11's lesson, the actual committed entry is `crates/enforcer-harness/adapters/*` (single star), verified by running the SAME dogfood-exclusion test pattern h11 used (a real walk of the repo root via `enforcer_config::resolve::resolve_profile_only` + `enforcer_scan::walk::{walk, IgnoreRules}`), plus a regression guard proving an unfiltered walk WOULD see the excluded files.
why: Without this, adding the ignoreFileGlobs entry in the exact prose form the workpack describes would have silently passed a naive review while doing nothing at scan time -- exactly the kind of dishonest-looking-honest gap the whole pack is about avoiding.
howToApply: Any future pack adding an `ignoreFileGlobs`/`ignoreDirs` entry in this codebase's CURRENT `enforcer-scan`/`enforcer-config` implementation must use single-star prefix form (`dir/*`) and should add the same two-test pattern (filtered walk = zero hits under the excluded prefix; unfiltered walk = nonzero hits) rather than trusting the glob string alone. This is still a latent defect in `walk.rs::glob_matches` (no real `**` support) -- worth a dedicated fix pass, but out of scope for any single rule-adding pack.

statement: This workspace's root `[workspace.lints]` denies `clippy::panic`, `clippy::unwrap_used`, and `clippy::expect_used` with NO exemption for `#[cfg(test)]` modules or `tests/*.rs` integration-test files -- `panic!("expected X, got {other:?}")` inside a test's `match`/`else` arm, or `.expect("...")` on a test-only `Option`/`Result`, both fail `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exactly like production code would. The workspace has no established `run_fixture_parity`-style helper for the 'assert this specific enum variant, fail the test otherwise' case.
why: h12's first draft used `match outcome { Variant { .. } => {...}, other => panic!("expected Variant, got {other:?}") }` in four places (two in `src/adapters/cyberskills/recorded.rs` unit tests, two in `tests/cyberskills_adapters.rs`) and `cargo clippy -p enforcer-harness --all-targets -- -D warnings` failed closed on all four before any workspace-wide check was even attempted.
howToApply: In this workspace, replace `match value { Wanted { field } => {...}, other => panic!(...) }` inside any `#[test]` fn with `let Wanted { field } = value else { return Err(format!("expected Wanted, got {value:?}").into()); };` -- requires the test fn to return `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (already the dominant convention in this codebase's test files) rather than bare `()`. Grep `panic!\(` and `\.expect\(` across any new test file before considering it done; `cargo clippy --all-targets` is the only way to catch this, `cargo test`/`cargo build` do not.

statement: A pre-existing, unrelated `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` failure exists on `origin/rust-build` tip (commit 73c668f, confirmed via `git stash` on a clean lane/h12 checkout before any h12 edits): `crates/enforcer-lang-cfml/tests/rule_registry.rs` (landed by commit 1da484c, `e-pack-cfml`) uses `.expect("crates/ parent")`, `.expect("repo root")`, `panic!("no registry record for `{rule_id}`")`, and `.expect("CF-ARCH-6.1 must be registered")` -- all four denied by the same `[workspace.lints]` policy documented in mem-h12-0002. This blocks any true workspace-wide `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` from ever passing until fixed, independent of any other pack's work.
why: h12's own gate requires `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean`; needed to distinguish 'my new code introduced a clippy failure' from 'the workspace already had one' before concluding h12 was done. Verified via `git stash` + `cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-cfml --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the unmodified tree, then `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude enforcer-lang-cfml -- -D warnings` (clean) to prove h12's own additions introduce zero new violations.
howToApply: Any pack that needs a genuinely clean `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (not just their own crate) should expect to hit this enforcer-lang-cfml failure until a dedicated fix lands (spawned as a separate task by h12, task_6e061b14). Do not assume a workspace-wide clippy failure is caused by your own current changes without first checking via `git stash`/a clean baseline run.

evidence.source: cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-cfml --all-targets -- -D warnings (on unmodified origin/rust-build tip)

statement: h12's `EngineFinding`/`RawRecorded` structs (crates/enforcer-harness/src/adapters/cyberskills/{seam,recorded}.rs) needed explicit `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to deserialize the fixture JSON's `ruleId`/`toolPresent`/`errorMessage` fields -- omitting it (the initial draft did) makes serde expect snake_case field names by default and every fixture-driven test fails with `missing field` decode errors, NOT a compile error, so it only surfaces at `cargo test` time.
why: This workspace's wire convention (documented in enforcer-domain/src/findings.rs) is camelCase JSON with snake_case Rust field names; every new serde struct that round-trips through fixture JSON in this workspace needs the derive attribute explicitly -- it is not a workspace-wide default (no `#[serde(rename_all = ...)]` at a container/module level).
howToApply: When adding a new `#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]`/`Serialize` struct that will parse or emit JSON fixtures/wire payloads in this workspace, ALWAYS add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on the struct up front (mirrors `enforcer_domain::findings::Finding`) rather than discovering the mismatch via failing fixture tests.

evidence.source: cargo test -p enforcer-harness adapters::cyberskills (initial run: 4 failures, all fixed by adding rename_all=camelCase)
